lessons.title: A club begins by the Douro
lessons.subtitle: FC Porto dates its activity to September 1893.

story.title: A founding date
story.body: FC Porto’s statutes identify a precise day when the club was founded and began its activity.

story.title: A city club
story.body: The legal document anchors the institution in Porto and records its original name.

facts.label: Foundation date
facts.prompt: In which year does UEFA list FC Porto as formed?
facts.scope: Founding year listed in UEFA club facts.
facts.evidence: UEFA lists FC Porto as formed in 1893.

facts.label: Nickname
facts.prompt: What nickname does UEFA give FC Porto?
facts.evidence: UEFA lists the nickname Dragões (The Dragons).

facts.label: European home record
facts.prompt: What score was Porto’s biggest home win in UEFA club competition, against Rabat Ajax in 1986?
facts.scope: Porto’s UEFA club competition record, 17 September 1986.
facts.evidence: UEFA records the 9–0 home win over Rabat Ajax on 17 September 1986.

lessons.title: The back-heel that changed Porto
lessons.subtitle: A late equaliser set up a first European Cup triumph.

story.title: Bayern led
story.body: In the 1987 European Cup final, Bayern Munich were ahead 1–0 as time ran down.

story.title: A sudden reversal
story.body: Rabah Madjer back-heeled the equaliser, then set up Juary four minutes later.

facts.label: Equaliser
facts.prompt: Who scored Porto’s equaliser against Bayern in the 1987 European Cup final?
facts.evidence: UEFA says Madjer back-heeled past Jean-Marie Pfaff with time running out.

facts.label: Goal technique
facts.prompt: How did Madjer beat Bayern goalkeeper Jean-Marie Pfaff for Porto’s equaliser?
facts.scope: The move that levelled the 1987 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes his equaliser as a back-heel beyond Pfaff.

facts.label: Winning assist
facts.prompt: Who did Madjer set up four minutes after his equaliser?
facts.scope: Porto’s winning goal in the 1987 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Madjer set up Filho Juary four minutes after his goal.

lessons.title: Derlei decides it in Seville
lessons.subtitle: Porto’s 2003 UEFA Cup final went to extra time.

story.title: A pendulum final
story.body: Celtic twice came back to level the score after Porto took the lead.

story.title: Silver-goal finish
story.body: Derlei scored again in the 115th minute to give Porto its first UEFA Cup.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Porto beat Celtic in the 2003 UEFA Cup final after extra time?
facts.scope: 2003 UEFA Cup final, after extra time.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Celtic 2–3 Porto after extra time.

facts.label: Winning goal time
facts.prompt: In which minute did Derlei score the extra-time winner against Celtic?
facts.scope: The decisive goal of the 2003 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA states Derlei scored after 115 minutes.

facts.label: Decision rule
facts.prompt: Under which unusual rule was the 2003 final decided?
facts.evidence: UEFA calls Porto the first team to win a trophy under the silver-goal rule.

lessons.title: Deco finds his footing
lessons.subtitle: After loans and setbacks, Porto became his springboard.

story.title: A difficult start
story.body: UEFA’s career account says Deco could not establish himself at Benfica and went on loan to Alverca and Salgueiros.

story.title: A new level
story.body: At Porto he won three Portuguese league titles and two major European competitions.

facts.label: Career turning point
facts.prompt: Which club did Deco join after his loan spells at Alverca and Salgueiros?
facts.scope: Deco’s move after spells away from Benfica.
facts.evidence: UEFA states he moved to Porto after the two loans.

facts.label: Porto league honours
facts.prompt: How many Portuguese league titles did Deco win with Porto, according to UEFA?
facts.evidence: UEFA lists three Portuguese league titles with Porto.

facts.label: Porto European honours
facts.prompt: Which two UEFA club competitions did Deco win with Porto?
answers: UEFA Cup and UEFA Champions League
distractors: Cup Winners’ Cup and UEFA Cup

value.display: UEFA Cup and UEFA Champions League
value.text: UEFA Cup and UEFA Champions League

facts.evidence: UEFA identifies Porto’s 2002/03 UEFA Cup and 2003/04 Champions League wins.

lessons.title: Deco’s pass opens the final
lessons.subtitle: A disguised through ball helped Porto regain the lead against Celtic.

story.title: Porto were level
story.body: In the 2003 UEFA Cup final, Celtic had equalised Porto’s first goal early in the second half. Neil Lennon was marking Deco man to man, so movement helped him find space.

story.title: Deco sees the run
story.body: His angled outside-of-the-right-foot pass sent Dmitri Alenichev through for a 2–1 lead.

facts.label: Assist recipient
facts.prompt: Who received Deco’s angled pass to put Porto 2–1 ahead in the 2003 UEFA Cup final?
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies Alenichev as the scorer after Deco’s pass.

facts.label: Pass technique
facts.prompt: Which part of his foot did Deco use for the assist to Alenichev in the 2003 UEFA Cup final?
facts.scope: The technique in his assist for Alenichev.
facts.evidence: Deco described clipping diagonally with the outside of his right foot.

facts.label: Man-marking challenge
facts.prompt: Which Celtic midfielder marked Deco man to man in the 2003 UEFA Cup final?
facts.evidence: Mourinho identifies Neil Lennon as Deco’s man-to-man marker.

lessons.title: A debut goal against Brazil
lessons.subtitle: Deco’s first Portugal appearance came against the country where he was born.

story.title: A new international shirt
story.body: Deco, born in Brazil, became a Portuguese citizen and was called up for Portugal in 2003.

story.title: An immediate impact
story.body: He came on as a substitute and scored a late free-kick winner against Brazil.

facts.label: Debut match result
facts.prompt: What was Portugal’s score against Brazil in Deco’s international debut?
facts.evidence: UEFA says he debuted against Brazil and scored in Portugal’s 2–1 win.

facts.label: Debut goal method
facts.prompt: How did Deco score the winning goal against Brazil?
facts.evidence: UEFA records his first Portugal goal as a free-kick winner.

facts.label: Goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Deco score the winner on his Portugal debut against Brazil in 2003?
facts.evidence: UEFA’s report on the Portugal–Brazil debut says he converted an 82nd-minute free kick.

lessons.title: Deco’s European awards double
lessons.subtitle: UEFA named him both its best midfielder and overall MVP for 2003/04.

story.title: A remarkable season
story.body: Deco helped Porto win the Champions League and was honoured at UEFA’s 2004 awards.

story.title: Two distinctions
story.body: He received both the Best Midfielder award and Most Valuable Player award.

facts.label: UEFA position award
facts.prompt: Which position award did Deco receive at UEFA’s 2004 European Football Awards?
facts.evidence: UEFA says he received Best Midfielder.

facts.label: Overall award
facts.prompt: What overall distinction did Deco also receive in 2004?
facts.evidence: UEFA reports he returned to accept the MVP award.

facts.label: Final goal
facts.prompt: Against which club did Deco score in the 2004 Champions League final?
facts.evidence: UEFA lists Deco’s goal at 71 minutes in Porto’s 3–0 final win over Monaco.

lessons.title: A long career in goal
lessons.subtitle: Baía’s career brought success in Portugal and Spain.

story.title: Two Porto spells
story.body: UEFA reports that Baía made 406 league appearances for Porto across two spells.

story.title: A wide honours list
story.body: He won club trophies in Portugal and Spain and earned 80 caps for Portugal.

facts.label: Porto league appearances
facts.prompt: How many league appearances did Vítor Baía make for Porto across his two spells?
facts.evidence: UEFA states he made 406 league appearances for Porto in two spells.

facts.label: International caps
facts.prompt: How many times was Baía capped by Portugal?
facts.evidence: UEFA’s retirement profile says he was capped 80 times.

facts.label: Barcelona honour
facts.prompt: Which European trophy did Baía win with Barcelona in 1997?
facts.evidence: UEFA says he won the 1997 Cup Winners’ Cup with Barcelona.

lessons.title: Baía shuts the door on Monaco
lessons.subtitle: His early intervention helped Porto through a tense final.

story.title: A dangerous break
story.body: Monaco captain Ludovic Giuly broke through in the opening minutes of the 2004 final.

story.title: Baía reads it
story.body: The Porto goalkeeper rushed out and made a sliding challenge before Giuly could finish.

facts.label: Attacker stopped
facts.prompt: Which Monaco player did Baía challenge early in the 2004 final?
facts.scope: Porto–Monaco Champions League final, within three minutes.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes Giuly racing clear and Baía making the sliding challenge.

facts.label: Intervention
facts.prompt: How did Vítor Baía stop Giuly’s early break in the 2004 Champions League final?
answers: Rushed out and made a sliding challenge
distractors: Blocked a header on the line

value.display: Rushed out and made a sliding challenge
value.text: Rushed out and made a sliding challenge

facts.evidence: UEFA says Baía raced out of his box for a crucial sliding challenge.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Porto’s 2004 final against Monaco?
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Porto beat Monaco 3–0.

lessons.title: A rare set of three European cups
lessons.subtitle: Baía completed a continental trophy treble with Porto in 2004.

story.title: Different competitions
story.body: He won the Cup Winners’ Cup with Barcelona before collecting the UEFA Cup with Porto.

story.title: The final piece
story.body: Porto’s 2004 Champions League victory completed the set. By retirement in 2007, his domestic collection also included eight Portuguese Super Cups.

facts.label: European trophy set
facts.prompt: Which three major European club competitions completed Baía’s continental trophy treble?
answers: Cup Winners’ Cup, UEFA Cup and Champions League
distractors: Champions League, Super Cup and Intercontinental Cup
UEFA Cup, Europa League and Super Cup
Cup Winners’ Cup, Intertoto Cup and Champions League

value.display: Cup Winners’ Cup, UEFA Cup and Champions League
value.text: Cup Winners’ Cup, UEFA Cup and Champions League

facts.scope: Baía’s trophy career through the 2004 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA calls this a hat-trick of continental titles and names the three competitions.

facts.label: Portuguese Super Cups
facts.prompt: How many Portuguese Super Cups had Vítor Baía won when he retired in 2007?
facts.scope: Completed career, UEFA retirement profile published 13 June 2007.
facts.evidence: UEFA lists eight Super Cups in Portugal in his retirement honours tally.

facts.label: Clean-sheet record
facts.prompt: In its 2013 profile, how many consecutive Portuguese top-flight minutes without conceding did UEFA credit to Vítor Baía?
facts.scope: Baía’s league clean-sheet record as reported by UEFA in 2013.
facts.evidence: UEFA records 1,191 minutes without conceding in Portugal’s top flight.

lessons.title: A keeper decorated across leagues
lessons.subtitle: Baía collected honours in Portugal and Spain and a UEFA award.

story.title: A Portuguese collection
story.body: UEFA’s career tally includes ten league titles, five domestic cups and eight Portuguese Super Cups.

story.title: Recognition as a goalkeeper
story.body: In 2004, UEFA’s European awards named Baía its Best Goalkeeper.

facts.label: Portuguese league titles
facts.prompt: How many Portuguese league titles did Baía win?
facts.scope: His completed club honours as of retirement.
facts.evidence: UEFA lists ten league titles in Portugal.

facts.label: Portuguese domestic cups
facts.prompt: How many Portuguese domestic cups did Baía win?
facts.scope: His completed honours as of retirement.
facts.evidence: UEFA lists five domestic cups in Portugal.

facts.label: UEFA award
facts.prompt: Which 2004 UEFA European Football Award did Baía receive?
facts.evidence: UEFA says Baía and Ricardo Carvalho were selected Best Goalkeeper and Best Defender respectively.

lessons.title: An ambitious club takes shape
lessons.subtitle: José Alvalade imagined Sporting as a major European club.

story.title: A breakaway in 1906
story.body: The club history says Alvalade and supporters left Campo Grande Foot-Ball Club over its social direction.

story.title: A broad sporting idea
story.body: Sporting began with five sports, not only football.

facts.label: Recognition year
facts.prompt: In which year was Sporting CP officially recognised?
facts.evidence: The club history says Sporting was officially recognised in May 1906.

facts.label: Founder
facts.prompt: Who voiced the ambition to make Sporting as great as Europe’s biggest clubs?
facts.evidence: The founding history attributes the statement to José Alvalade.

facts.label: Original sports
facts.prompt: How many sports did Sporting’s founding group begin with?
facts.evidence: Sporting’s history lists five founding sports: tennis, football, athletics, gymnastics and tug-of-war.

lessons.title: Sporting wins after a replay
lessons.subtitle: João Morais’s corner settled the 1964 Cup Winners’ Cup final replay.

story.title: One draw was not enough
story.body: Sporting and MTK Budapest drew 3–3 after extra time in Brussels.

story.title: A direct finish
story.body: In Antwerp two days later, Morais scored directly from a corner in the 1–0 win.

facts.label: Replay result
facts.prompt: What was the score when Sporting beat MTK in the 1964 final replay?
facts.scope: Cup Winners’ Cup final replay, Antwerp.
facts.evidence: UEFA lists the replay as MTK 0–1 Sporting.

facts.label: Replay scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Sporting’s only goal in the replay?
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies João Pedro Morais as the 20th-minute scorer.

facts.label: Goal method
facts.prompt: How did Morais score the replay winner?
distractors: A header from a free kick
facts.evidence: UEFA says the goal came direct from a corner.

lessons.title: A final played at home
lessons.subtitle: Sporting led the 2005 UEFA Cup final at half-time before CSKA turned it around.

story.title: Rogério strikes first
story.body: Sporting’s official history says Rogério gave the hosts a 1–0 lead before the interval.

story.title: CSKA rallies
story.body: The Russian side scored three second-half goals to win 3–1 at José Alvalade.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score in Sporting’s 2005 UEFA Cup final against CSKA Moscow?
facts.evidence: Sporting’s official history reports a 1–3 loss to CSKA.

facts.label: Sporting scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Sporting’s opening goal in the 2005 final?
facts.scope: Sporting’s first-half goal in the final.
facts.evidence: Sporting says Rogério put the team ahead in the 29th minute.

facts.label: Final venue
facts.prompt: At which stadium did Sporting host the 2005 UEFA Cup final?
facts.evidence: The club says the final was played at the new Estádio José Alvalade.

lessons.title: A first-team door opens
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo’s Sporting debut came at 17 in a European qualifier.

story.title: A teenager earns his chance
story.body: Sporting used Ronaldo in its Champions League qualifier against Inter.

story.title: The first senior appearance
story.body: He entered in the second half of the 0–0 first leg on 14 August 2002.

facts.label: Sporting debut date
facts.prompt: On what date did Cristiano Ronaldo make his first-team debut for Sporting?
facts.evidence: UEFA dates his Sporting debut to 14 August 2002.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Sporting face in Ronaldo’s first-team debut?
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies the match as Sporting–Inter in Champions League qualifying.

facts.label: Debut score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Ronaldo’s debut match for Sporting?
facts.evidence: UEFA says the first leg finished goalless.

lessons.title: A goal before the debut
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo scored his first Sporting goal in a pre-season friendly against Betis.

story.title: A glimpse in pre-season
story.body: UEFA recalls his goal came in a 3–2 friendly victory shortly before the Inter qualifier.

story.title: A difficult angle
story.body: He beat the goalkeeper and curled the ball into the top corner from outside the area.

facts.label: First Sporting goal opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did Ronaldo score his first Sporting goal?
facts.evidence: UEFA reports his first Sporting goal came in a friendly against Betis.

facts.label: Friendly score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Sporting’s friendly win in which Ronaldo first scored?
facts.scope: The match containing Ronaldo’s first Sporting goal.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies the friendly as a 3–2 win against Betis.

facts.label: Goal finish
facts.prompt: How did Ronaldo finish his first Sporting goal against Betis?
answers: Curled a shot into the top corner from outside the area

value.display: Curled a shot into the top corner from outside the area
value.text: Curled a shot into the top corner from outside the area

facts.scope: His pre-season goal before the 2002/03 campaign.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes him beating the keeper and curling a difficult-angle shot into the top corner.

lessons.title: The Sporting audition in Manchester
lessons.subtitle: A friendly against United helped trigger Ronaldo’s transfer.

story.title: A preseason showcase
story.body: Sporting played Manchester United in a friendly in August 2003.

story.title: A transfer follows
story.body: UEFA records that United completed Ronaldo’s signing days later, for €17.5 million.

facts.label: United signing date
facts.prompt: On what date did Manchester United complete Ronaldo’s signing?
facts.evidence: UEFA reports United completed the deal on 12 August 2003.

facts.label: Transfer fee
facts.prompt: What fee did UEFA report Manchester United agreed for Ronaldo?
facts.evidence: UEFA states the agreed fee was €17.5m, payable over two years.

facts.label: Contract length
facts.prompt: How long was the contract Ronaldo signed with Manchester United?
facts.scope: The original United contract in August 2003.
facts.evidence: UEFA says the 18-year-old signed a five-year contract.

lessons.title: Five Champions League wins by 2018
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo became the first player to reach five titles.

story.title: A first medal at United
story.body: Ronaldo began his collection with Manchester United in 2008.

story.title: A new milestone in Kyiv
story.body: After Real Madrid beat Liverpool 3–1 in the 2018 final, he became the first player to win five Champions League finals.

facts.label: Five-time winner
facts.prompt: How many Champions League titles had Ronaldo won after the 2018 final?
facts.scope: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Champions League title record as of the 2018 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA says he became the first player to win the competition five times.

facts.label: Milestone final
facts.prompt: Which final made Ronaldo the first player to win five Champions League finals?
facts.scope: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Champions League title record as of the 2018 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA says Madrid’s 3–1 defeat of Liverpool in Kyiv made five titles.

facts.label: First winning club
facts.prompt: With which club did Ronaldo begin his Champions League winners’ medal collection?
facts.scope: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Champions League title record as of the 2018 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA states his first title came with Manchester United in 2008.

lessons.title: Six seasons before Spain
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s Sporting years launched an illustrious club and international career.

story.title: A youth international
story.body: UEFA highlights his 1989 European Under-16 title with Portugal.

story.title: A first club cup
story.body: He spent six years at Sporting and won the 1995 Portuguese Cup before moving to Barcelona.

facts.label: Sporting tenure
facts.prompt: How long did Figo spend at Sporting before joining Barcelona?
facts.evidence: UEFA states he spent six years at Sporting.

facts.label: First major club trophy
facts.prompt: Which major club trophy did Figo first win with Sporting in 1995?
facts.evidence: UEFA says the 1995 Portuguese Cup was his first major club trophy.

facts.label: Youth international title
facts.prompt: Which tournament did Figo help Portugal win in 1989?
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies Portugal’s 1989 Under-16 title.

lessons.title: A Sporting debut and farewell
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s first-team debut and final appearance for Sporting both came against Marítimo.

story.title: First appearance
story.body: Sporting records Figo’s first-team debut on 1 April 1990 against Marítimo.

story.title: A final cup match
story.body: Five years later, his Sporting farewell also came against Marítimo in the Portuguese Cup final.

facts.label: First-team debut date
facts.prompt: When did Figo make his first-team debut for Sporting?
facts.evidence: Sporting records his debut against Marítimo on 1 April 1990.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Sporting face for Figo’s first-team debut?
facts.evidence: Sporting says the debut came against Marítimo.

facts.label: Farewell opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Sporting face in Figo’s farewell match, the 1995 Portuguese Cup final?
facts.scope: His final Sporting appearance in June 1995.
facts.evidence: Sporting says Marítimo was the opponent in his farewell cup final.

lessons.title: Portugal’s comeback against England
lessons.subtitle: Figo helped spark a 3–2 EURO 2000 comeback after England scored twice.

story.title: A difficult start
story.body: Portugal fell 2–0 behind in its opening group match against England.

story.title: Figo responds
story.body: His long-range strike pulled one back, and Portugal went on to win 3–2.

facts.label: Comeback score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when Portugal came back to beat England at EURO 2000?
facts.evidence: UEFA titles its account Portugal 3–2 England and describes the comeback.

facts.label: Figo’s goal
facts.prompt: What did Figo’s goal do in Portugal’s match against England?
facts.evidence: UEFA’s match report identifies Figo’s strike as Portugal’s first goal after England scored twice.

facts.label: Individual honour
facts.prompt: Which major individual award did Figo win in 2000?
facts.evidence: UEFA states he received the Ballon d’Or in 2000.

lessons.title: A record for Portugal
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s international career ended with a national appearance record.

story.title: Fifteen years
story.body: UEFA describes Figo as a Portugal mainstay for 15 years.

story.title: A record total
story.body: He finished with 127 caps, then a record for the national team.

facts.label: Portugal caps
facts.prompt: How many senior caps did Figo earn for Portugal?
facts.evidence: UEFA’s profile records 127 caps, a Portugal record at the time.

facts.label: 2001 award
facts.prompt: Which global player award did Figo win in 2001?
facts.evidence: UEFA says he won FIFA World Player one year after the 2000 Ballon d’Or.

facts.label: European club title
facts.prompt: In which season did Figo win the Champions League with Real Madrid?
facts.evidence: UEFA says he won the Champions League in 2002 during his Madrid tenure.
